activities.caption: place the marker on the age where the risk reaches 1 in 100
activities.name: gmMaternalPlace

config.prompt: Trisomy-21 risk runs about 1 in 1,250 at age 25. Place the marker on the maternal age where it reaches roughly 1 in 100:
config.why: About 1 in 100 at age 40 — mechanical, because ova rest in meiosis from before birth, so nondisjunction risk accumulates with time.

activities.anchor: means the foetus has the condition
activities.caption: one line of the prenatal note skips the confirmation step
activities.name: gmNiptSpot

config.prompt: A note on non-invasive prenatal testing — one line is wrong. Click it:
lines: NIPT reads cell-free DNA, much of which comes from the placenta.
Confined placental mosaicism, vanishing twins and maternal conditions can produce positive results for a chromosomally normal foetus.
A positive screen is a diagnosis — clinical decisions can follow it directly.
Sensitivity for the common trisomies is excellent, but predictive value depends on rarity.
A positive screen requires diagnostic confirmation before any decision.
config.correction: NIPT is a screening test: a positive screen still requires confirmation by diagnostic testing (amniocentesis or CVS) before any clinical decision.
config.why: The pipeline's logic is a high-sensitivity screen followed by diagnostic confirmation of what matters — collapsing the two steps is where prenatal-genomics errors live.

activities.anchor: Genotype is not destiny by three mechanisms
activities.caption: file each softening mechanism
activities.name: gmPhenoBuckets

config.prompt: Three mechanisms stand between genotype and phenotype — file each finding:

items.label: the same variant giving very different risks across carriers
hundreds of variants each adding a sliver, summed into a risk score
imprinting — the same chromosomal region, opposite outcomes depending on parent of origin
diet methylating a gene and changing coat colour in the agouti-mouse experiments
risk scores built on European-ancestry data misperforming elsewhere

config.why: The clinic's craft is translating variants into quantified, actionable probabilities — including the discipline to say "we don't know yet".

activities.anchor: The clinical act is translating a variant into a quantified, actionable probability
activities.caption: pair each genotype with its risk architecture
activities.name: gmPenetranceMatch

config.prompt: Three architectures of "having the gene" — pair each with its risk shape:

pairs.right: elevated lifetime risk, on the order of 55–70% for breast cancer, modifiable by screening and surgery

config.why: Variant reports are probabilities, not sentences — the architecture of the risk is part of the result.

config.root: A prescription meets a metaboliser genotype. Walk the check.

start.text: The patient is an ultra-rapid CYP2D6 metaboliser and an opioid prodrug activated by that enzyme is on the chart. What follows?

choices.label: Alert: activation is excessive — overdose risk; choose a different analgesic
Standard dosing — the genotype applies only to new drugs
choices.feedback: Genes controlling metabolism decide whether a medication works, does nothing, or harms.

fast.text: Fatalities — including in breastfed infants — drove this drug's withdrawal from paediatric use in many countries. The implemented list runs wider: warfarin dosing (CYP2C9 and VKORC1), the HLA-B*57:01 test before abacavir, TPMT testing before mercaptopurine.

ignore.text: Variants sort patients into poor, intermediate, normal and ultra-rapid metabolisers — some loss-of-function alleles reach a fifth or more of certain populations.

config.why: Poor, intermediate, normal, ultra-rapid — the metaboliser classes are sorted before the prescription is written.

activities.anchor: Resistance is the genomic lesson's recursive edge
activities.caption: rebuild the tumour-genome treatment loop
activities.name: gmCancerOrder

config.prompt: Treatment as an iterative loop — drag the passes into order:
items: Sequence the tumour's genome and find the driver
Match the targeted drug: EGFR, BRAF, HER2, or the BCR-ABL inhibitor
The tumour evolves under drug pressure
Resistance mutations (EGFR T790M and successors) emerge
Re-biopsy and switch to a second-generation inhibitor — the loop repeats
config.why: Each pass re-reads the genome; circulating tumour DNA is extending the loop to monitoring without needles in tumours.

activities.anchor: an individual rare disease is hopeless to diagnose by pattern recognition
activities.caption: call the diagnostic yield
activities.name: gmYieldEstimate

config.prompt: Sequencing the exome tests thousands of Mendelian candidates at once. In suspected Mendelian disease, roughly what share of expert-centre exome tests return a diagnosis?
config.why: Diagnostic yield runs in the 25–40% range at expert centres — and each diagnosis ends an odyssey that often lasted five to ten years of specialist visits.
